summary: Selene Compass is an interactive 3D decision-support web platform designed to evaluate and compare potential landing sites near the lunar South Pole. By combining real NASA terrain and astronomical datasets (LOLA and JPL Horizons), it calculates a weighted Safety Score (0–100) based on slope, solar illumination, and Earth visibility, helping mission planners identify safer landing zones quickly.
details:
What it does: Selene Compass is an interactive 3D lunar South Pole landing site navigator. It allows users to explore candidate landing regions (such as Shackleton Rim), inspect terrain topography, visualize safety zones through color-coded layers (Safe, Caution, Hazardous, Permanent Shadow), and compare multiple sites side-by-side.How it works: The platform integrates lunar elevation models and celestial position data to evaluate three key environmental factors: terrain slope, solar illumination duration, and direct line-of-sight visibility to Earth. Users can adjust the weight of each factor according to their mission priorities, and the system dynamically computes an overall Safety Score from 0 to 100.Benefits & Goals: Traditional site evaluation requires analyzing complex, separate scientific datasets manually. Selene Compass unifies these parameters into one accessible visual interface, making preliminary site assessment faster, clearer, and more organized for researchers, students, and mission planners. Note: It serves as a decision-support and comparison tool rather than an official landing certification.Tools & Technologies Used: Built using React, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Router, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide React, and deployed online via Vercel.

Full Video Demonstration:https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kGfojpYs7vbCcdF3Xdk3KJKs_MCspJZt/view?usp=drivesdk
